_note: Structural at-a-glance facts for Chennai's urban water supply, primarily extracted from the ADB Chennai Climate Resilient Water Security and Sewerage Project (CCRWSSP) Initial Environmental Examination (March 2026, Project 59311-001). The CCRWSSP IEE documents Chennai's existing multi-source supply (5 WTPs + 3 DSPs, 1,544 MLD avg supply against 2,287 MLD installed treatment capacity) and the proposed Ring Main System (RMS) - a 97.9 km circular bulk transmission ring connecting all major WTPs/DSPs to eliminate the city's source-zone fragmentation. Numbers refresh per ADB project publication.

_view_overrides.subtitle: Structural numbers from CMWSSB and the ADB Chennai Climate Resilient Water Security and Sewerage Project (CCRWSSP). Refreshed when new engineering documents are published.
_view_overrides.demand_caption: Chennai's installed capacity already exceeds intermediate-year demand. The structural risk is not headline supply gap but distribution fragmentation - each WTP/DSP today commands its own zone with no balancing. The proposed Ring Main System ties all 8 sources into one continuous loop, redistributing supply across zones.

supply_chain: Surface reservoirs (Puzhal, Poondi, Cholavaram, Chembarambakkam, Veeranam) + Krishna canal + Cauvery + Sea water
5 freshwater WTPs (Kilpauk, Puzhal, Surapet, Chembarambakkam, Vadakuthu) + 3 desal plants (Minjur, Nemmeli I, Nemmeli II)
115 km transmission mains (up to 1,200 mm MS pipelines)
7 ground-level Clear Water Reservoirs (CWRs) + 16 major Water Distribution Stations (WDSs)
85 WDSs total feeding 5,247 km distribution network

current_supply_mix_mld.note: Kilpauk is Chennai's oldest WTP. Receives Puzhal tank storage + Krishna water through Poondi-Red Hills route.

current_supply_mix_mld.note: Krishna water (Telugu Ganga Project, 339.84 MCM allocation) is conveyed through Poondi-Red Hills before treatment.
Currently under rehabilitation per CCRWSSP IEE March 2026.
Chennai's largest single WTP. Lake also drains the 2015 flood story.

current_supply_mix_mld.supplies: Inter-zone bulk supply via long-distance main
current_supply_mix_mld.note: Cauvery river system source. ~230 km transmission from Cuddalore district.

current_supply_mix_mld.scheme: Bay of Bengal -> Nemmeli DSP I (2013)
Bay of Bengal -> Nemmeli DSP II (2024)

_supply_total_note: 1,687 MLD is sum of installed treatment capacity across active WTPs/DSPs. CCRWSSP IEE Table 1 reports the city's average actual supply at 1,544 MLD (capacity utilisation ~67% of 2,287 MLD if Surapet rehab and Perur are included). The gap reflects raw-water availability, plant downtime, and Surapet rehabilitation rather than nominal capacity.

wtps_summary.planned_additions_breakdown: Perur DSP (+400 MLD, expected 2027) + Orathur/Manimangalam Lake WTP proposed by CMA (+200 MLD)

distribution._note: Distribution figures from CCRWSSP IEE March 2026 page 10 (paragraph 21). Chennai's distribution differs from Madurai's: 16 GCC administrative zones (not Madurai's 28 distribution zones), 85 WDSs (water distribution stations), 7 ground-level Clear Water Reservoirs (CWRs), 16 major WDSs as backbone, all fed by 115 km of large-diameter transmission mains.

connections._total_note: Per CCRWSSP IEE: '9.3 lakh domestic and non-domestic service connections (as of March 2022)'. The IEE's parenthetical '(equivalent to 1,000,000)' is a rounding error - 9.3 lakh = 930,000, not 1 million.

distribution._population_note: Per CCRWSSP IEE para 14: 'Chennai's water supply system... serves a population of over 8.5 million'. Covers all 16 GCC administrative zones across 426 km^2.

demand._population_design_note: CCRWSSP IEE uses 8.5 million as current population served; demand projections are at GCC area level rather than per-capita.
demand._demand_2034_note: 2034 not directly published in IEE; using IEE's 2042 intermediate projection (1,496 MLD) as nearest available proxy. Used for compatibility with the supply-overview tile schema.
demand._demand_gap_note: Chennai's existing 1,544 MLD avg supply already exceeds the 2042 intermediate-year demand of 1,496 MLD. The structural risk is not headline supply gap but distribution fragmentation (each WTP has its own commanding area with no balancing) - which the proposed Ring Main System addresses. By 2057 ultimate-year demand of 1,766 MLD, capacity additions (Perur 400 + CMA 200 = +600 MLD) will be needed.

allocation_context._note: Chennai's water sources span four states/basins: Krishna (AP, via Telugu Ganga), Cauvery (TN, via Veeranam), local Tamil Nadu reservoirs, and the Bay of Bengal. No single-source dependency comparable to Madurai's Mullaperiyar - but Krishna allocations have historically been politically contested.
allocation_context.krishna_allocation_note: Telugu Ganga Project commissioned 1996. Allocation is variable - actual deliveries depend on AP releases.
allocation_context.veeranam_note: Cauvery river system. Long-distance transmission (~230 km) from Cuddalore district.
allocation_context._desalination_share_note: 350 MLD desal / 1,687 MLD total = 21%. Among the highest desal share of any large Indian city. Will rise to ~33% post Perur (400 MLD).
allocation_context.tracked_reservoirs_note: Combined live capacity of Poondi + Cholavaram + Red Hills + Chembarambakkam reservoirs (CMWSSB daily reservoir bulletin). These are what Neer Vazhvu's days-of-water-left hero on /chennai operates against.

rms_project._note: The Ring Main System (RMS) is the headline subproject of the CCRWSSP. It addresses the 'source-based zones' fragmentation problem - each WTP currently supplies its own independent area with no interconnections, so a single source failure (drought, plant shutdown, power issue) cripples its zone. RMS creates a unified circular bulk transmission line tying all 8 WTPs/DSPs into one resilient network.
rms_project._new_ugts_capacity: 6 x 1 ML + 1 x 0.5 ML = 6.5 ML new clear-water storage
rms_project.surge_tanks_breakdown: 5 RCC one-way + 3 MS two-way surge shafts
rms_project._pipe_carrying_bridges_note: 17 along ring main (6 within CRZ requiring CRZ clearance) + 7 along transmission mains (all 7 in CRZ). Cross Retteri Lake, Adyar River, Buckingham Canal, Cooum River, Captain Cotton Canal, South Boag Road Nalla, Otteri Nalla, Veerangal Odai, Kosasthalaiyar River.
rms_project.scada: New SCADA system with sensors for real-time flow/pressure/pumping/reservoir-level monitoring; one Master Control Center to be added

reference_figures.caption: Sources of water supply in Chennai - the geographic spread across reservoirs (Poondi, Cholavaram, Red Hills, Chembarambakkam), Veeranam (Cauvery), Krishna canal arrival, and DSPs at Minjur and Nemmeli (Figure 3 of CCRWSSP IEE).
Proposed ring main alignment connecting all WTPs and DSPs (Figure 4 of CCRWSSP IEE) - the unified circular transmission backbone that ties source-based zones into one resilient network.
Schematic Flow of Water diagram for existing water supply (Figure 5 of CCRWSSP IEE) - shows the source-WTP-CWR-WDS-distribution chain end to end.

Line diagram showing existing and proposed RMS components (Figure 7 of CCRWSSP IEE) - a topological view of how the new ring, feeder mains, transmission mains, surge tanks and UGTs fit into the existing system.

ccrwssp.scope: Climate-resilient water security + sewerage. Includes RMS (97.9 km ring main, 8 surge tanks, 7 new UGTs, 7 pump replacements, 24 pipe-carrying bridges), 10-year performance-based O&M contract, NRW reduction, SCADA + digital twin, robotic CCTV/sonar sewer inspection, gender career-scholarship program
ccrwssp.status_per_iee: Draft IEE - field reconnaissance + secondary data + stakeholder consultations
ccrwssp.key_outputs: Resilient unified bulk transmission, equitable inter-zone distribution, real-time SCADA monitoring, reduced NRW, asset management modernization
